title: Do you know some movies that handle the subject of clouds in an original way (let's discuss)

commenti.body:
The Gods Must Be Crazy - the edge of the world

Nope - a cloud that doesn't move

Brazil - the flying dream sequences with the fake clouds

Heaven Can Wait (1978) - the cloudy Heaven

Truman Show - clouds painted on the wall

Aviator - they have to wait for clouds to film aerial sequences

Raiders of the Lost Ark - special effect clouds when they find the ark (and lots of 80s movies copied it)

Empire Strikes Back - Cloud City
Oh thanks a lot !! I hadn't thought about some of these films ! I will look at them !

In Ran there’s a lot of Cloud stuff but I haven’t seen the movie enough or read about it to really unpack their usage or meaning.. I just know there’s a bunch of shots of clouds.


Gus Van Sant famously loves clouds… can’t get enough of them.
Thanks a lot ! I will look at Van Sant !

Not a movie, but China Meiville's shot Story Polynia uses the motif of cloud-as-iceberg in a really original way to tell a story about adventure, disaster, and climate.  


Hope you enjoy!
Thanks a lot ! I will look at it 😊

In Ran, the sky starts out perfectly clear, but gradually becomes cloudier and darker as the land falls into chaos. Lots of shots of the skyline contrasted with the battlefields.
Yeah, I get that much but wondered if there’s wasn’t more too it. Though you’re definitely right in how it reflects the mood of the movie.

I remember them being pretty prevalent in My Own Private Idaho (which I think is his best work and a personal favorite.)

They also appear in his almost shot for shot remake of Psycho (they’re one of the few additions in the movie that make it not a shot for shot remake and I always wondered if there was more too it or if he was adding his signature style to the film as part of the sort of “meta-conversation” it’s in with the original.)

They are non-narrative documentaries, so I'm not quite sure if they fit, but Baraka and Koyaanisqatsi both have incredible moving time-lapses of clouds. As a weather & film enthusiast they are some of the most beautiful and extraordinary timelapse shots I've ever seen. 

The particular scene from Baraka is available on YT here (linked right where the cloud shots start): https://youtu.be/m6MLQgoepXY?t=1033

Now, a timelapse of clouds isn't exactly anything new. But the shots here are incredible: high cirrus/notilucent clouds captured with stars during a moving timelapse at night, clouds flowing over mountains like water. You see them in a totally new light. Not quite sure if it counts for your essay, but I don't see why it couldn't.

There's a certain cloud formation that pops up over and over again in the films of the anime director Mamoru Hosoda. I forget it's name, but basically he said that the reason he always showed it was twofold

1. As a quick shorthand to show the season (summer)
2. As an expression of the characters' transformation/development. To this end, he cuts to them whenever the character grows in knowledge and/or skill.
Thanks you a lot ! You are right this is perfect thanks for ur testimony
Ohhh interesting ! I will look at it thanks
XD Thanks a lot !

I think Koyaanisqatsi has some more extended cloud timelapses, Chronos (the precursor to Baraka) also has a few as well I believe. Anyway, if it interests you at all, I think these films are all necessary viewing; many people are put off by the non-narrative nature but the soundtracks and incredible cinematography all done in 65mm is nothing short of extraordinary and keep you engaged. The two sequels to Koyaanisqatsi are not as good but worth a watch if you enjoyed the first. Oh, and somehow I almost forgot Samsara, the more recent sequel to Baraka. I've not seen it for some time but it probably also has some cloud timelapses because they are just so mesmerizing.
